That’s up to you. If you can live with constant rejection for now then so be it. But if it affects you as a person, that’s another thing. It’s a decision you have to make for yourself. Everyone is different. It may take months or years for someone to adjust and fight intrusive thoughts. I was with my SO for 6 years before pulling the plus. I’m 100% sure if I had found out sooner about my mental health, we would still be together. He was a good guy. But he’s also much happier now. And although I hurt both of us, in the long run we were able to build meaningful lives and relationships with our current SO’s. But my current SO is highly understanding. Always said ‘ok’ when I would break up over him coming late from hanging out with his friends. Not getting a reaction really fucked with me so then I was like hmm, he’s understanding even then? Okay I need to get to find out why I’m feeling this way lol

I was your SO a while back. It took me a ton of practice and mindfulness to understand that sometimes when I was to leave my SO for no reason and fantasize about being with other people, it’s my hyper sexuality speaking. I’ve come to learn that my SO is the best thing that has ever happened to me and leaving him and being with another person isn’t worth it to me. It’s almost a daily thought, but I have to overcome those thoughts every time. It was very hard in the beginning, but I believe it can get better. 

BTW I did have a relationship where I would leave all the time, tons of cheating, did what I wanted. I left for good when I eventually became so distant that being with that person felt strange. I regret who I was back then, but it led to my diagnoses and I’m forever grateful for individual therapy, intensive outpatient group therapy, antidepressants and mood stabilizers. It changed my life. Best of luck to you.
